properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 20 at 4:01PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
At 401 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Palomas, moving east at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Truth or Consequences, Engle, Palomas, Cutter, City of Elephant
Butte, Williamsburg, Ash Canyon, Lower Palomas Canyon, Upper Palomas
Canyon, and Elephant Butte Lake.

This includes Interstate 25 in New Mexico between mile markers 68 and
76.
properties.instruction: If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 20 at 2:54PM MST until October 22 at 10:00PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Southeast Arizona, including the following
areas, Galiuro and Pinaleno Mountains, Upper Gila River Valley and
White Mountains of Graham and Greenlee Counties.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A strong weather system approaching the area will bring scattered
showers and thunderstorms on Wednesday and widespread showers and
scattered thunderstorms on Thursday. Moderate to locally heavy
rainfall both days with Thursday having the higher potential for
localized rainfall rates of 1 to 2 inches per hour.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 20 at 5:18PM AST until October 21 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...North-facing beaches of Culebra.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH WEDNESDAY AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 20 at 5:18PM AST until October 21 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8 to
10 feet. For the High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip
currents.

* WHERE...For the High Surf Advisory the most vulnerable areas for
high surf and beach erosion include Pinones along Road 187,
Parcelas Suarez, Villas del Mar, and Villa Christiana in Loiza;
Fortuna in Luquillo; Pueblo and Tamarindo in Aguadilla; Barrio
Obrero, Pueblo and Jareaito in Arecibo; Las Boca in Barceloneta;
Machuca in Manati; Puerto Nuevo in Vega Baja; Ocean Park in San
Juan; and Barrio Espinal in Aguada. For High Rip Current Risk,
the most vulnerable areas are the exposed northwesterly and
north- facing beaches. For the High Rip Current Risk, the most
vulnerable areas are the exposed northwesterly and north-facing
beaches. Breaking waves can continue to reach 7 to 9 feet
tonight.

* WHEN...The High Surf Advisory remains until 6 PM AST this
evening. The High Rip Current Risk remains through Wednesday
afternoon.

* IMPACTS...For the High Surf Advisory, high waves that can wash
over jetties and sweep people and pets onto jagged rocks. Rough
surf may also knock you down. Large breaking waves will result
in localized beach/dune structure erosion and dangerous swimming
conditions. For the High Rip Current Risk, rip currents can
sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water,
where it becomes difficult to return to safety.
properties.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches in
the advisory area, producing localized beach erosion and
dangerous swimming conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.headline: High Wind Watch issued October 20 at 1:11PM AKDT until October 24 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...South to southeast winds 35 to 50 mph with gusts up to 70
mph possible.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta, and Northern Bristol Bay Coast.

* WHEN...From Friday morning through Saturday morning.

* IMPACTS...High winds could move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong, storm force Bering front is on track
to sweep the Aleutian Chain and arrive to the Kuskokwim Delta/coast
and Bristol Bay coast Friday morning. There is currently medium to
high confidence (60 to 80 percent chance) of wind gusts exceeding
60 mph for these locations.
properties.instruction:
A high wind watch means there is potential for a hazardous high wind
event. Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates on this
situation. Fasten loose objects or shelter objects in a safe location
prior to the onset of winds.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 20 at 1:00PM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Multiple periods of heavy rain are expected for the Icy Strait
corridor and northeast Gulf Coast, including the following
communities: Yakutat, Elfin Cove, Pelican, Gustavus, Juneau. Elevated
gusty winds are expected alongside this heavier rainfall, with the
strongest winds from the southwest expected late this morning into
this afternoon. Prolonged periods of moderate to heavy rain will
produce significant river rises with the potential for at least minor
flooding in Juneau and Gustavus. Ponding of water in low-lying areas
is also possible.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The following areas, Eastern Gulf Coast and Northeast Gulf
Coast. This includes the cities of Elfin Cove And Pelican.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.
Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rain totals for the Elfin Cove and Pelican area through this
evening range between 3-4 inches, with greater than 6 inches
possible at elevations greater than 1000 ft. Coinciding with high
rain rates, possibly exceeding 0.3 inches per hour, elevated wind
gusts greater than 40 mph are expected at elevations greater than
500 ft.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could

vessel for hazardous conditions.
